item.title: Eisenkot, Liberman express "full confidence" in forming a stable govt in Israel
item.description: Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot and Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Liberman expressed “full confidence” in their ability to form a stable government for a full four-year term following a meeting on ...
item.content:encoded:
Eisenkot, Liberman express "full confidence" in forming a stable govt in Israel Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot and Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Liberman expressed “full confidence” in their ability to form a stable government for a full four-year term following a meeting on Monday, amid ongoing disagreements over the formation of Israel's next government, according to The Times of Israel. ANI | Updated: 09-11-2026 21:03 IST | Created: 09-11-2026 21:03 IST

Yisrael Beiteinu leader Avigdor Liberman (L) and Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot (R) (File Photo/ Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot and Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Liberman expressed “full confidence” in their ability to form a stable government for a full four-year term following a meeting on Monday, amid ongoing disagreements over the formation of Israel's next government, according to The Times of Israel. In a statement following the meeting on Monday, the Yashar party called the discussions between the two leaders “constructive and productive”. “Both expressed full confidence in their ability to form a stable government for a full four-year term,” the party said in a statement, as reported by The Times of Israel. The meeting came amid tensions between the two leaders over Eisenkot's coalition-building options. Liberman has ruled out supporting a minority government or one dependent on Arab-led parties, while signalling his willingness to negotiate with ultra-Orthodox factions. However, as per the Times of Israel, the statement did not indicate whether the two leaders had resolved their differences or reached any concrete agreements regarding the formation of the next government. The meeting comes amid ongoing political negotiations in Israel following Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot receiving the mandate from President Isaac Herzog to form the country's next government. Meanwhile, ahead of the swearing-in of Israel's new Knesset on Tuesday, November 10, Yair Golan, leader of Israeli Democrats, expressed pride in his party's newly elected team, highlighting its members as "principled, courageous, talented fighters" who would work towards changing Israel's political landscape. In a post on X, Golan said, "Tomorrow, the new Knesset will be sworn in, and I look with great pride at our team--the Democrats’ team. Proud of every woman and man elected to represent us, and of the path they took to reach this moment." Eisenkot formally received the mandate on Sunday after securing recommendations from 67 members of the 120-member Knesset during consultations with political factions. His support included lawmakers from Yashar, B'Yachad, The Democrats, Yisrael Beiteinu and Arab-led parties. He has 28 days to form a government, with Herzog authorised to grant an additional extension of up to 14 days if required. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
US-Israel security pact set to halve direct military aid post-2028 under evolving five-year framework: Report  New details reveal US military aid to Israel will not end immediately, but will instead be halved to a five-year package after 2028. Negotiators aim to finalise the memorandum of understanding before January, navigating domestic political hurdles and potential congressional appropriations challenges. ANI | Updated: 09-11-2026 14:57 IST | Created: 09-11-2026 14:57 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

American military assistance to Israel will not terminate immediately under a forthcoming security memorandum of understanding, with new details uncovered by Ynetnews indicating that direct aid will instead be reduced by roughly half by restricting its duration to a five-year window following 2028 rather than the traditional decade-long span. These revelations surface approximately a week after US President Donald Trump unexpectedly stated that he and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had agreed to halt American military aid by the close of the year, leaving Israeli negotiating teams bewildered by the pronouncement, as reported by Ynetnews. A senior Israeli official assessed that Trump's declaration was driven primarily by domestic political calculations to assist Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan against Democratic challenger Abdul El-Sayed, though the strategy ultimately proved unsuccessful as El-Sayed secured victory, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate, according to Ynetnews. During a Fox News appearance on Election Day, Trump stated, "We were giving them $4 billion. We are, but it gets cut off at the end of the year." He additionally noted that Netanyahu had previously raised the concept of phasing out assistance on the grounds that Israel had evolved into a prosperous nation no longer requiring such backing. Nevertheless, the evolving framework does not contemplate an immediate stoppage, with current assistance remaining fully active through 2028 under the prevailing model that grants USD 3.3 billion yearly in Foreign Military Financing alongside USD 500 million for joint defence research, Ynetnews noted. Under the revised terms under discussion by teams representing US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Israel's Defence Ministry, annual funding levels would remain comparable for a shortened five-year period totalling roughly USD 16.5 billion before direct military provisions cease. Meanwhile, American allocations dedicated to collaborative air and missile defence advancement are anticipated to climb from the present USD 500 million annually to an amount yet to be finalised. Furthermore, a senior Israeli official familiar with the diplomatic exchanges observed that numerous members of Congress resist lowering assistance due to domestic economic factors, given that the vast majority of funds flow directly back into American manufacturing plants and local state economies, as detailed by Ynetnews. "We are moving here from a model of aid to a model of partnership," the senior Israeli official stated, adding, "It is important to remember that most of the security assistance remains in America and contributes to the American economy. Cutting it would also hurt American industries and require adjustments." While negotiators aim to conclude the pact prior to the new Congress convening in January, Israeli planners remain wary regarding annual congressional appropriation hurdles and potential political friction. Officials have acknowledged that future government compositions and leadership figures will heavily influence legislative backing in Washington, Ynetnews reported. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Iran defends two-day proposal for peace talks after US rejects conditions Reuters | Updated: 09-11-2026 14:41 IST | Created: 09-11-2026 14:41 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Iran defended a proposal on Monday to restart peace talks in as few as two days as the most reasonable offer on the table, after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called some of Iran's conditions "outrageous and ridiculous". "Is it unreasonable that Iran demands that US illegal sanctions and its naval blockade must be lifted before negotiations start and that the war should end on all fronts?" Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei told a weekly press conference in response to Rubio's remarks. Iran has made the offer to shorten the time to restart talks from an earlier seven-day proposal, which calls for Washington to first meet conditions including halting hostilities, lifting a blockade and waiving sanctions. Baghaei also said US pressure on Iraq to close most of its borders with Iran should not affect bilateral ties with Baghdad, after Iraq's foreign minister said Washington was pushing for such a move. Baghaei dismissed a US military task force aimed at restricting Iran's land trade as a diversion following President Donald Trump's Republicans' losses in midterm elections.
